corpus_baselines.note: All three baselines are evaluated on the SAME induction-relevant positions as the model, not on the full corpus. Uniform=1/vocab_size. Char-mode=always predict mode char. Bigram=predict argmax P(c_{t+1}|c_t) from training corpus.

conclusion: The previous-token head (L0H7) identified on synthetic tasks generalizes perfectly to natural language. Content-matching head predictions are partially supported: L1H6 contributes but L2H0 and L2H4 do not.
detailed_conclusion: Model accuracy on induction positions: 1.000. Three baselines on the same positions: uniform=0.0154, char-mode (predict ' ')=0.2920, bigram=0.0760. Best baseline=0.2920. Induction advantage=0.7080.  L0H7 ablation drops induction advantage by 0.620 (raw accuracy drop 0.620): previous-token head prediction CONFIRMED.  L1H6 ablation drops advantage by 0.038: content-matching head CONFIRMED.  Content-matching predictions for ['L2H0', 'L2H4'] are NOT supported (advantage drops: L2H0: 0.002, L2H4: 0.010).
paper_claim: The model achieves 1.000 accuracy on induction-relevant positions, versus 0.2920 for the best non-induction baseline (bigram predictor: 0.0760), yielding an induction advantage of 0.7080. Ablating L0H7 (previous-token head) reduces this advantage by 0.620, confirming its role. The previous-token head identified on synthetic tasks generalizes perfectly to natural language. Content-matching head predictions are partially supported: L1H6 contributes but L2H0 and L2H4 do not.
